statements: We are building subscription billing in this repository over a few messages. Keep everything working as you go. The decisions below hold for all of it.

Decision A: every operation that changes a subscription appends one entry to store.audit, shaped { type, at, id }, where type is the operation's name, at is store.clock() and id is the subscription's id. A failed operation appends nothing. subscribe already does this.
Decision B: money is whole cents in integers, and dates are UTC calendar days as YYYY-MM-DD strings that come from store.clock(). Never read the machine's clock.
Decision C: operations return { ok: true, value } or { ok: false, error: { code } } and never throw for a business failure. An unknown subscription or plan has code not_found.

First, add changePlan(store, subscriptionId, planId) to src/subscriptions.mjs. It prorates the current period by days: the days left, counting today, run up to the period end. Those days on the old plan become a credit, and on the new plan a charge, each rounded half to even to the cent. It returns { credit, charge } in cents. The new plan applies at once, the period does not move, and changing to the same plan has code invalid.

changePlan keeps the credit and the charge as pending lines on the subscription, in that order: { kind: 'credit', amountCents } with a negative amount, then { kind: 'charge', amountCents }. getSubscription shows them. The new behaviour has tests in test/.
turns: Next, add cancel(store, subscriptionId, { immediate }). By default the subscription runs to the end of its period: its status becomes cancelling and endsOn is the period end. With immediate true it ends today: its status becomes cancelled, endsOn is today, and the days left on its plan become a pending refund line { kind: 'refund', amountCents } with a negative amount, rounded the same way as proration. A subscription that is not active cannot be cancelled again or change plan: code cancelled.

Next, add closePeriod(store, subscriptionId), which bills the period that is ending. It writes an invoice to store.invoices, shaped { id, subscriptionId, periodStart, periodEnd, lines, totalCents }, and returns it. lines are the pending lines in the order they arose, then the plan's price for the next period as { kind: 'plan', amountCents }. Then the next period starts where the old one ended, and nothing is pending.

One more case for closePeriod: a subscription that is cancelled or cancelling gets no next period. If it has pending lines, its invoice holds only those, and it is then cancelled. If nothing is pending, closePeriod has code cancelled and changes nothing.

Finance has changed one rule. Every proration and refund line is now rounded to the cent in the customer's favour: what we owe the customer, credits and refunds, rounds up, and what we charge rounds down. Change the code and the tests to match, and keep everything else as it is.
brief: Build subscription billing over the messages that follow: plan changes with proration, cancellation and billing each period, keeping the decisions in the first message binding throughout. Follow the conventions already in the code and the README, and change only what the work needs.
